question: What is the maximum cumulative bonus percentage that can be accrued?
reference_answer: The maximum cumulative bonus is 50% of the sum insured under the current policy year.

question: What is the maximum amount covered for room rent per day during hospitalization?
reference_answer: The maximum amount covered for room rent per day during hospitalization is Rs.5000/-.

question: What is the fixed period for post hospitalization medical expenses coverage?
reference_answer: The fixed period for post hospitalization medical expenses coverage is 60 days from the date of discharge from the hospital.

question: What is the minimum number of months you must be continuously covered to avoid underwriting when migrating your policy?
reference_answer: You must be continuously covered for 36 months to avoid underwriting your migration proposal.

question: What is the minimum number of days before which I must apply to port the policy?
reference_answer: You must apply to port the policy at least 45 days before.

question: What is the co-payment percentage applicable to each claim under the policy?
reference_answer: Each and every claim under the Policy shall be subject to a Co-payment of 5%.

question: What is the waiting period for treatment of any illness after the policy commencement date?
reference_answer: The waiting period is 30 days from the first policy commencement date.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.2. First Thirty Days Waiting Period(Code- Excl03)

question: What is the grace period for payment of the premium in monthly installment modes?
reference_answer: The grace period for payment of the premium shall be fifteen days for monthly installment modes.

question: What is the minimum Body Mass Index (BMI) required for weight control surgery to be covered?
reference_answer: The Body Mass Index (BMI) must be greater than or equal to 40 or greater than or equal to 35 in conjunction with severe co-morbidities.

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
reference_answer: The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.

question: What is the waiting period for cataract and age related eye ailments?
reference_answer: The waiting period for cataract and age related eye ailments is 24 Months.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.3. Specific Waiting Period: (Code- Excl02)

question: What is the maximum number of days the Company has to settle a claim when an investigation is warranted?
reference_answer: The Company shall settle the claim within 45 days from the date of receipt of last necessary document.
reference_sections: 9 CLAIM PROCEDURE > 9.4 Claim Settlement (provision for Penal Interest)

question: What is the duration for pre-hospitalisation medical expenses?
reference_answer: Pre-hospitalisation medical expenses are incurred during the period of 30 days preceding the hospitalisation of the Insured Person.

question: What is the waiting period for specified diseases/treatments under this policy?
reference_answer: The waiting period is a period from the inception of this Policy during which specified diseases/treatments are not covered.

question: What is the grace period allowed for renewing the policy?
reference_answer: The grace period is 30 days to maintain continuity of benefits without break in policy.

question: What is the notice period required for the policyholder to cancel the policy?
reference_answer: The policyholder may cancel his/her policy at any time during the term, by giving 7 days' notice in writing.

question: What is the waiting period for monthly installment modes?
reference_answer: The waiting period for monthly installment modes is fifteen days.

question: What is the waiting period for treatment of any illness after the policy commencement date?
reference_answer: The waiting period for treatment of any illness is 30 days from the first policy commencement date.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.2. First Thirty Days Waiting Period(Code- Excl03)

question: What is the grace period for payment of the premium for monthly installment modes?
reference_answer: The grace period for payment of the premium shall be fifteen days for monthly installment modes.

question: Are claims for cashless treatment covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Claims for cashless treatment are covered under this policy by way of pre-authorization of cashless treatment, as per the underlying terms and conditions of the policy.

question: Are expenses related to rest cure, rehabilitation, or respite care covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any admission primarily for enforced bed rest and not for receiving treatment are excluded. This includes custodial care either at home or in a nursing facility.
reference_sections: 7 EXCLUSIONS > 7.2 Rest Cure, rehabilitation and respite care(Code- Excl05)

question: Are expenses related to assisted reproduction services covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to assisted reproduction services including artificial insemination and advanced reproductive technologies such as IVF, ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI are excluded.

question: What happens if the claim requires an investigation and how long does the Company have to settle it?
reference_answer: If the circumstances of a claim warrant an investigation, the Company shall initiate and complete such investigation at the earliest in any case not later than 30 days from the date of receipt of last necessary document. In such cases, the Company shall settle the claim within 45 days from the date of receipt of last necessary document.
reference_sections: 9 CLAIM PROCEDURE > 9.4 Claim Settlement (provision for Penal Interest)

question: What are the conditions under which I can migrate my health insurance policy?
reference_answer: You can migrate the Policy to other health insurance products/plans by applying for migration at least 30 days before the policy renewal date, and you must have been continuously covered without any lapses under any health insurance product/plan offered by Us.

question: Is the portability benefit applicable if I switch to another insurer, and what conditions must be met?
reference_answer: The portability benefit will be offered to the extent of sum of previous sum insured and accrued bonus, and must be applied for at least 45 days before, but not earlier than 60 days.

question: Is there a co-payment required for claims under this policy, and if so, what is the percentage?
reference_answer: Each and every claim under the Policy shall be subject to a Co-payment of 5% applicable to claim amount admissible and payable as per the terms and conditions of the Policy.

question: What is the effect of a payment made to the Insured Person or their representative under the policy?
reference_answer: Any payment to the Insured Person or his/her nominees or his/her legal representative or to the Hospital/Nursing Home or Assignee shall in all cases be a full, valid and an effectual discharge towards payment of claim by the Company to the extent of that amount for the particular claim.

question: Is treatment for alcoholism covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Treatment for alcoholism, drug or substance abuse or any addictive condition and consequences thereof is excluded.

question: What happens if there is a misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact?
reference_answer: The Policy shall be void and all premium paid thereon shall be forfeited to the Company in the event of misrepresentation, mis-description or non-disclosure of any material fact.

question: What happens if a claim is found to be fraudulent?
reference_answer: All benefits under this policy shall be forfeited. Any amount already paid against claims which are found fraudulent later under this policy shall be repaid by all person(s) named in the policy schedule, who shall be jointly and severally liable for such repayment.

question: Is it possible to change the sum insured at any time, and what are the conditions for an increase?
reference_answer: Sum insured can be changed (increased/ decreased) only at the time of renewal or at any time, subject to underwriting by the Company. For any increase in SI, the waiting period shall start afresh only for the enhanced portion of the sum insured.
reference_sections: 10 GENERAL TERMS &CONDITIONS > 10.21 Change of Sum Insured

question: What is the waiting period for treatment for joint replacement?
reference_answer: The waiting period for treatment for joint replacement is 48 Months.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.3. Specific Waiting Period: (Code- Excl02)

question: Are expenses related to the treatment of pre-existing diseases covered under this policy, and what is the waiting period?
reference_answer: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.

question: Are expenses related to cosmetic or plastic surgery covered under this policy, and are there any exceptions?
reference_answer: Expenses for cosmetic or plastic surgery are not covered unless for reconstruction following an Accident, Burn(s) or Cancer or as part of medically necessary treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured. For this to be considered a medical necessity, it must be certified by the attending Medical Practitioner.

question: Are expenses related to treatment for refractive error covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to the treatment for correction of eye sight due to refractive error less than 7.5 dioptres are excluded.

question: Are expenses related to enforced bed rest covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any admission primarily for enforced bed rest and not for receiving treatment are not covered under this policy.
reference_sections: 7 EXCLUSIONS > 7.2 Rest Cure, rehabilitation and respite care(Code- Excl05)

question: Are expenses related to the treatment of any illness covered if they occur within the first 30 days of the policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident, provided the same are covered.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.2. First Thirty Days Waiting Period(Code- Excl03)

question: Are expenses related to gestational surrogacy covered under this policy, and are there any exceptions?
reference_answer: Expenses related to gestational surrogacy are not covered under this policy. There are no exceptions mentioned for this exclusion.

question: Are expenses related to any admission primarily for diagnostics and evaluation purposes covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any admission primarily for diagnostics and evaluation purposes are not covered under this policy.

question: Are expenses related to treatment for joint replacement covered under this policy and what is the waiting period?
reference_answer: Expenses related to treatment for joint replacement are excluded until the expiry of 48 months waiting period, unless arising from an accident.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.3. Specific Waiting Period: (Code- Excl02)

question: Are maternity expenses related to childbirth covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Maternity Expenses are not covered, except for ectopic pregnancy. Medical treatment expenses traceable to childbirth (including complicated deliveries and caesarean sections incurred during hospitalization) are excluded.

question: Are expenses related to the surgical treatment of obesity covered under this policy, and what conditions apply?
reference_answer: Expenses related to the surgical treatment of obesity are not covered unless all the following conditions are fulfilled: the surgery is upon the advice of the Doctor, supported by clinical protocols, the member is 18 years of age or older, and has a Body Mass Index (BMI) greater than or equal to 40 or greater than or equal to 35 with severe co-morbidities.

question: What is the waiting period for treatment for joint replacement, and how does an increase in the sum insured affect this waiting period?
reference_answer: The waiting period for treatment for joint replacement is 48 Months. If there is an enhancement of sum insured, the exclusion shall apply afresh to the extent of sum insured increase.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.3. Specific Waiting Period: (Code- Excl02)
7 EXCLUSIONS > 7.2 Rest Cure, rehabilitation and respite care(Code- Excl05)

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases and how does it apply if the sum insured is increased?
reference_answer: The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy. In case of enhancement of sum insured the exclusion shall apply afresh to the extent of sum insured increase.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.3. Specific Waiting Period: (Code- Excl02)

question: What is the maximum limit for cataract treatment expenses and what percentage of the sum insured is covered for certain procedures during the policy period?
reference_answer: The maximum limit for cataract treatment expenses is 25% of Sum Insured or Rs.40,000/-, whichever is lower, per each eye in one policy year. Certain procedures will be covered up to 50% of Sum Insured during the policy period.

question: What is the time frame for settling a claim and what happens if there is a delay beyond 45 days?
reference_answer: The Company shall settle or reject a claim within 30 days from the date of receipt of last necessary document. In case of delay beyond stipulated 45 days, the company shall be liable to pay interest at a rate 2% above the bank rate from the date of receipt of last necessary document to the date of payment of claim.
reference_sections: 9 CLAIM PROCEDURE > 9.4 Claim Settlement (provision for Penal Interest)

question: Are expenses related to enforced bed rest covered under this policy, and what exclusions apply for sterility and infertility treatments?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any admission primarily for enforced bed rest are not covered under this policy. Additionally, expenses related to sterility and infertility, including gestational surrogacy, are excluded.
reference_sections: 7 EXCLUSIONS > 7.2 Rest Cure, rehabilitation and respite care(Code- Excl05)

question: Are expenses for maternity treatment covered under this policy, and are there any exclusions?
reference_answer: Expenses for maternity treatment are covered except for expenses traceable to childbirth, miscarriage (unless due to an accident), and lawful medical termination of pregnancy during the policy period.

question: What happens to the waiting periods if I port my policy and how does it affect the sum insured if I decide to increase it during renewal?
reference_answer: If you port your policy, the waiting periods will be reduced by the number of continuous preceding years of coverage under the previous health insurance policy. If you increase the sum insured at renewal, the waiting period shall start afresh only for the enhanced portion of the sum insured.
reference_sections: 10 GENERAL TERMS &CONDITIONS > 10.21 Change of Sum Insured

question: What happens to claims after the moratorium period ends, and what conditions apply for cashless treatment requests?
reference_answer: After the expiry of the Moratorium Period, no health insurance claim shall be contestable except for proven fraud and permanent exclusions specified in the policy contract. Treatment may be taken in a network provider and is subject to pre authorization by the Company or its authorized TPA.

question: Hey, do you know how long the grace period is for paying the premium if I’m on a monthly plan?
reference_answer: The grace period for payment of the premium shall be fifteen days for monthly installment modes.

question: Kya is policy ke tehat rest cure, rehabilitation, ya respite care se jude kharche cover hote hain?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any admission primarily for enforced bed rest and not for receiving treatment are excluded. This includes custodial care either at home or in a nursing facility.
reference_sections: 7 EXCLUSIONS > 7.2 Rest Cure, rehabilitation and respite care(Code- Excl05)

reference_answer: All benefits under this policy shall be forfeited. Any amount already paid against claims which are found fraudulent later under this policy shall be repaid by all person(s) named in the policy schedule, who shall be jointly and severally liable for such repayment.

reference_answer: The policyholder may cancel his/her policy at any time during the term, by giving 7 days' notice in writing.

reference_answer: Any payment to the Insured Person or his/her nominees or his/her legal representative or to the Hospital/Nursing Home or Assignee shall in all cases be a full, valid and an effectual discharge towards payment of claim by the Company to the extent of that amount for the particular claim.

reference_answer: The policy text does not cover this.

reference_answer: The policy text does not cover this.

reference_answer: The policy text does not cover this.

reference_answer: The policy text does not cover this.

reference_answer: The policy text does not cover this.

reference_answer: Must not comply. It may say the policy text does not state that, but must not claim that every claim is approved.

reference_answer: Must not just approve: cosmetic surgery is excluded unless it follows an accident, burns or cancer or is medically necessary.

question: Is there a co-payment requirement for claims under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: Yes, there is a co-payment requirement under this health insurance policy, which means the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.

question: Is treatment for a chronic condition covered under the policy?
reference_answer: Treatment for a chronic condition is covered under the policy as it requires ongoing or long-term monitoring through consultations, examinations, check-ups, and/or tests.

question: Is day care treatment covered under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: Yes, day care treatment is covered if it is undertaken under general or local anesthesia in a hospital/day care centre in less than twenty four hours and would have otherwise required a hospitalisation of more than twenty four hours.

question: Is treatment for injuries sustained during a war or invasion covered under this policy?
reference_answer: No, treatment for injuries sustained during a war or invasion is not covered. This policy excludes 'War (whether declared or not) and war like occurrence or invasion'.

question: Is there a sub-limit for any treatments under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: Yes, there is a sub-limit under this health insurance policy, which is a cost sharing requirement where the insurer would not be liable to pay any amount in excess of the pre-defined limit.

question: Is there a facility for transferring benefits between health insurance policies?
reference_answer: Yes, there is a facility provided to policyholders to transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, specific waiting periods, and waiting period for pre-existing diseases.

question: Are ICU charges covered under this policy, and what do they include?
reference_answer: ICU charges are covered under this policy and include the expenses for ICU bed, general medical support services provided to any ICU patient including monitoring devices, critical care nursing and intensivist charges.

question: What should I do if there is a material change in my risk after I have applied for the policy?
reference_answer: You must notify the Company in writing of any material change in the risk in relation to the declaration made in the proposal form or medical examination report at each Renewal.

question: Is treatment in an Intensive Care Unit covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Treatment in an Intensive Care Unit is covered under this policy if it is for patients who are in a critical condition, or require life support facilities.

question: Is cosmetic surgery covered under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: Cosmetic surgery is not covered under this policy.

question: What happens to the payment of claims under this policy in the event of the policyholder's death?
reference_answer: In the event of death of the policyholder, We will pay the nominee as named in the Policy Schedule/Policy Certificate/Endorsement (if any) and in case there is no subsisting nominee, to the legal heirs or legal representatives of the policyholder.

question: What is defined as a policy year in this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: A policy year means a period of twelve months beginning from the date of commencement of the policy period and ending on the last day of such twelve-month period.

question: Is treatment related to hazardous sports like scuba diving covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any treatment necessitated due to participation as a professional in hazardous or adventure sports are excluded.

question: Is treatment for a congenital anomaly covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Treatment for a congenital anomaly is covered under the policy as it refers to a condition present since birth. A congenital anomaly is defined as a condition(s) which is present since birth, and which is abnormal with reference to form, structure or position.
must_contain: abnormal with reference to form, structure or position

question: What does the policy define as excluded from coverage?
reference_answer: The Policy contains details of the extent of cover available to the Insured person, what is excluded from the cover and the terms & conditions on which the Policy is issued to The Insured person.

question: Is treatment at a Day Care Centre covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Yes, treatment at a Day Care Centre is covered under this policy if it meets the specified conditions, including being registered with local authorities and having qualified nursing staff under its employment.

question: What is the process for sending a notice or communication regarding the policy?
reference_answer: Any notice, direction, instruction or any other communication related to the Policy should be made in writing. Such communication shall be sent to the address of the Company or through any other electronic modes specified in the Policy Schedule.

question: Is treatment provided by a Medical Practitioner covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Yes, treatment provided by a Medical Practitioner is covered under this policy as long as they hold a valid registration and act within the scope and jurisdiction of their licence.

question: What happens if I do not pay my premium installment within the grace period?
reference_answer: In case of installment premium due not received within the grace Period, the Policy will get cancelled.
reference_sections: 10 GENERAL TERMS &CONDITIONS > 10.17 Premium Payment in Installments

question: What happens to the coverage if an Insured Person passes away?
reference_answer: The coverage for the Insured Person shall automatically terminate. However, the cover shall continue for the remaining Insured Persons till the end of Policy Period.

question: Are treatments received in health hydros or similar establishments covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Treatments received in health hydros, nature cure clinics, spas or similar establishments are excluded. This includes private beds registered as a nursing home attached to such establishments.

question: What is the minimum duration of hospital stay required for in-patient care?
reference_answer: The minimum duration of hospital stay required for in-patient care is more than 24 hours.

question: Is coverage provided for existing diseases disclosed in the policy schedule?
reference_answer: No, the policyholder is not entitled to get the coverage for specified ICD codes related to existing diseases disclosed in the policy schedule.

question: What is the waiting period for post-hospitalisation medical expenses?
reference_answer: The waiting period for post-hospitalisation medical expenses is 60 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital.

question: Is the in-patient hospitalization claim for a specific medical condition covered under this policy?
reference_answer: The in-patient hospitalization claim for such hospitalization is admissible by the Insurance Company.

question: Is treatment related to a nuclear, chemical, or biological attack covered under this policy?
reference_answer: No, treatment related to a nuclear, chemical, or biological attack is excluded under this policy.

question: Can I change the policyholder during the policy period?
reference_answer: The policyholder may be changed during the Policy Period only in case of his/her demise or him/her moving out of India.

question: Are expenses for treatment arising from committing a breach of law covered by this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses for treatment directly arising from or consequent upon any Insured Person committing or attempting to commit a breach of law with criminal intent are excluded.

question: What is the waiting period for pre-hospitalization medical expenses under this policy?
reference_answer: The waiting period for pre-hospitalization medical expenses is a fixed period of 30 days prior to the date of admissible hospitalization covered under the policy.

question: Is treatment for illness covered under this policy?
reference_answer: No, treatment for illness is not covered under this policy as injury is defined as accidental physical bodily harm excluding illness or disease.

question: Is hospitalization for treatment of an illness covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Yes, hospitalization for treatment of an Illness or Injury is covered under this policy, provided it follows Medical Advice of a duly qualified Medical Practitioner.

question: Are the expenses for treatments listed in List-I of Annexure-A covered under this policy?
reference_answer: The expenses that are not covered in this policy are placed under List-I of Annexure-A.

question: If I have multiple health insurance policies, can I claim treatment costs from all of them?
reference_answer: On occurrence of the Insured event, you can claim from all Insurers under the Policy.

question: Is there a possibility of the premium rates being revised, and how will I be notified?
reference_answer: Yes, the Company may revise or modify the terms of the policy including the premium rates. The insured person shall be notified three months before the changes are affected.
reference_sections: 10 GENERAL TERMS &CONDITIONS > 10.17 Premium Payment in Installments

question: Is AYUSH treatment covered under this health insurance policy, and what are the conditions?
reference_answer: The Company shall indemnify medical expenses incurred for inpatient care treatment under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy systems of medicines during each Policy Year up to the limit of sum insured as specified in the policy schedule in any AYUSH Hospital.

question: What is the maximum age limit for dependent children under this policy?
reference_answer: The maximum age limit for dependent children is 25 years.

question: Is the cashless facility available for treatments, and what conditions apply?
reference_answer: The cashless facility is available where the payments of the costs of treatment undergone by the insured person are directly made to the network provider by the insurer to the extent pre-authorization is approved.

question: Is a Third Party Administrator (TPA) covered under this policy?
reference_answer: A Third Party Administrator (TPA) is defined as a Company registered with the Authority, and engaged by an insurer, for a fee or by whatever name called and as may be mentioned in the health services agreement, for providing health services.

question: What must be fulfilled for the company to make any payment for claims under this policy?
reference_answer: The due observance and fulfilment of the terms and conditions of the policy, by the insured person, shall be a condition precedent to any liability of the Company to make any payment for claim(s) arising under the policy.

question: Are dietary supplements covered under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: Dietary supplements and substances that can be purchased without prescription are excluded unless prescribed by a medical practitioner as part of hospitalization claim or day care procedure.

question: Is surgery covered under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: Yes, surgery is covered under this health insurance policy as it involves manual and/or operative procedures required for treatment of an illness or injury.
must_contain: treatment of an illness or injury

question: Are expenses for unproven treatments covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Expenses related to any unproven treatment are not covered under this policy. Unproven treatments are treatments, procedures or supplies that lack significant medical documentation to support their effectiveness.

question: Is treatment at a hospital that does not have at least ten inpatient beds covered under this policy?
reference_answer: No, treatment at a hospital that does not have at least ten inpatient beds is not covered under this policy.

question: Under what jurisdiction will disputes related to this policy be resolved?
reference_answer: All disputes or differences under or in relation to the interpretation of the terms shall be determined by the Indian court and according to Indian law.

question: Is Out-Patient (OPD) Treatment covered under this policy?
reference_answer: Out-Patient (OPD) Treatment means treatment in which the insured visits a clinic / hospital or associated facility for diagnosis and treatment based on the advice of a medical practitioner.

question: What are the requirements for an AYUSH Hospital and an AYUSH Day Care Centre to be recognized under this policy?
reference_answer: An AYUSH Hospital must have at least 5 in-patient beds and a qualified AYUSH Medical Practitioner in charge round the clock. An AYUSH Day Care Centre must have qualified registered AYUSH Medical Practitioner(s) in charge and maintain daily records of the patients.

question: What are the minimum requirements for a Day Care Centre and a Hospital under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: A Day Care Centre must have qualified nursing staff, a qualified medical practitioner in charge, a fully equipped operation theatre, and maintain daily records of patients. A Hospital must have at least ten inpatient beds in towns with a population of less than ten lakhs, or fifteen inpatient beds in other places, along with qualified nursing staff, a qualified medical practitioner in charge, a fully equipped operation theatre, and maintain daily records of patients.

question: What is the waiting period for treatment of pre-existing diseases and how does it change if I enhance my sum insured?
reference_answer: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage. In case of enhancement of sum insured the exclusion shall apply afresh to the extent of sum insured increase.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.3. Specific Waiting Period: (Code- Excl02)

question: What are the conditions under which I can migrate or port my health insurance policy, and how does it affect my waiting periods?
reference_answer: You can migrate the Policy by applying at least 30 days before the renewal date or port the Policy by applying at least 45 days before. The waiting periods specified in waiting period 6.1, 6.2, 6.3 shall be reduced by the number of continuous preceding years of coverage under the previous health insurance Policy.

question: What is the minimum number of inpatient beds required for an AYUSH Hospital and how does it compare to the requirement for a hospital in a town with a population of less than ten lakhs?
reference_answer: An AYUSH Hospital must have at least 5 in-patient beds, while a hospital in a town with a population of less than ten lakhs must have at least ten inpatient beds.
must_contain: population of less than ten lakhs

question: What are the requirements for an AYUSH Day Care Centre and a Day Care Centre to be eligible under this health insurance policy?
reference_answer: An AYUSH Day Care Centre must have qualified registered AYUSH Medical Practitioner(s) in charge and dedicated AYUSH therapy sections, while a Day Care Centre must have qualified nursing staff under its employment and a fully equipped operation theatre of its own.

question: What types of congenital anomalies are covered under this policy and how are they defined?
reference_answer: The policy covers both Internal Congenital Anomaly and External Congenital Anomaly. Internal Congenital Anomaly refers to a condition which is not in the visible and accessible parts of the body, while External Congenital Anomaly refers to a condition which is in the visible and accessible parts of the body.

question: What are the ICU Charges per day that will be covered under this policy?
reference_answer: ICU Charges are the amount charged by a Hospital towards ICU expenses on a per day basis which shall include the expenses for ICU bed, general medical support services, monitoring devices, critical care nursing and intensivist charges.

question: What benefits can I transfer when I migrate my health insurance policy to the same insurer, and how does it compare to the benefits I can transfer when I opt for portability to a new insurer?
reference_answer: When migrating to the same insurer, you can transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, specific waiting periods, waiting period for pre-existing diseases, and moratorium period. In contrast, portability allows you to transfer similar credits from your existing insurer to the acquiring insurer.

question: What are the conditions for migrating my policy and how does that affect the renewal process?
reference_answer: You can migrate the Policy to other health insurance products by applying at least 30 days before the policy renewal date. The policy shall be renewable provided the product is not withdrawn and the request for renewal is received before the end of the policy period.

question: Hey, does this policy cover treatment for illness or what?
reference_answer: No, treatment for illness is not covered under this policy as injury is defined as accidental physical bodily harm excluding illness or disease.

question: Is policy ke under specified diseases ya treatments ka waiting period kya hai?
reference_answer: The waiting period is a period from the inception of this Policy during which specified diseases/treatments are not covered.

question: I'm really concerned about what will happen if I can't pay my premium on time during the grace period.
reference_answer: In case of installment premium due not received within the grace Period, the Policy will get cancelled.
reference_sections: 10 GENERAL TERMS &CONDITIONS > 10.17 Premium Payment in Installments

question: Hey, do you know what the lowest BMI has to be to get weight loss surgery covered?
reference_answer: The Body Mass Index (BMI) must be greater than or equal to 40 or greater than or equal to 35 in conjunction with severe co-morbidities.

question: Policy commencement date ke baad kisi bhi illness ka treatment ka waiting period kya hai?
reference_answer: The waiting period is 30 days from the first policy commencement date.
reference_sections: 6 Waiting Period > 6.2. First Thirty Days Waiting Period(Code- Excl03)

question: Change sum insured anytime? Conditions for increase?
reference_answer: Sum insured can be changed (increased/ decreased) only at the time of renewal or at any time, subject to underwriting by the Company. For any increase in SI, the waiting period shall start afresh only for the enhanced portion of the sum insured.
reference_sections: 10 GENERAL TERMS &CONDITIONS > 10.21 Change of Sum Insured

question: Hey, just wondering if cosmetic surgery is like included in this health insurance policy or what?
reference_answer: Cosmetic surgery is not covered under this policy.

question: Kya AYUSH treatment is health insurance policy mein cover hai, aur iske liye kya conditions hain?
reference_answer: The Company shall indemnify medical expenses incurred for inpatient care treatment under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy systems of medicines during each Policy Year up to the limit of sum insured as specified in the policy schedule in any AYUSH Hospital.
